messages.text: Let's focus on the staggered geometry, as it gives some improvement already

I’ll focus the larger sample and revised calibration on the staggered geometry. I’ll use the existing 10k events for development, reserve 20k fresh events for independent validation, and keep the original geometry results as the reference.

I’m using the project’s coordination and validation workflows again. The Spack preflight reports changed setup and lockfile fingerprints, so I’ll reverify the runtime before launching jobs. There is about 375 GiB free; the measured output size leaves enough room for the 120k-event staggered campaign and a disk reserve.

Completed the **staggered-only study: 100k training + 20k independent validation electrons**, using 12 DDSim threads.

On the same validation sample:

| Calibration | σ(R)/⟨R⟩ |
|---|---:|
| Historical 10k model | 31.34% |
| Retrained linear model | 31.32% |
| Revised spline model | **30.21%** |

The revised calibration gives a modest improvement. Its global mean response is **1.003**, but energy-dependent bias and substantial sector-seam losses remain.

Peak transport memory was **2.67 GiB**; ROOT output used **152.5 GB**, with no trimming needed. All 22 tests passed; independent review found no material issue.

[Draft PR #137](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/137) · [Report](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/codex/ecal-staggered-highstat-calibration/docs/validation/ecal-highstat/README.md) · [Vector SVG](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/codex/ecal-staggered-highstat-calibration/docs/validation/ecal-highstat/results/angular-comparison.svg)
